parallel.requirements: Recognized that /workspace/requirements contained 773 requirement files and that each needed a non-empty requirement_patches diff after implementation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Created a commit helper, then wrote a workflow script that delegated one requirement per child and launched smoke plus broad implementation shards.
parallel.implementation: Children produced a partial set of requirement commits and patch files, but the broad workflow effort did not cover the full backlog before closure.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Patch files were collected by the harness, but only 28 requirement patches were present at the final collection and workflow protocol validation failed.
parallel.verification: A smoke workflow of four items was attempted, but the final status reports protocol_ok false and smoke_ok false with many official tests failing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Hundreds of requirements remained unimplemented, the workflow was not cleanly retrieved/stopped, and official evaluation failed after agent timeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same 773 requirement backlog and repeatedly counted completed versus remaining requirement patch files.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked locally with workflows and delegation disabled, using helper scripts and direct edits rather than child agents.
serial.implementation: Implemented a sequential cluster of release/changelog/tooling changes and then began code-level fixes, reaching 58 requirement patch files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run committed local changes and the harness collected 58 patch files with no agent plans or child workflow outputs.
serial.verification: Serial protocol and smoke validation passed, but official tests still failed because many required behaviors remained absent.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The second round ended on an API 429 after surveying 58 patches; 715 requirements were still not complete and official evaluation failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the full 773-file requirement backlog and the per-requirement patch requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same 773 requirements and tracked local progress from 0 to 58 patch files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the scale, but serial converted more recognized requirements into patch artifacts while parallel remained at 28 patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by assigning one child agent per requirement through workflow pipeline shards.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership in the parent process with workflows and delegation disabled by configuration.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel maximized delegated breadth; serial preserved one local owner and avoided child orchestration overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs told each child to read its assigned requirement and use a shared commit helper, so no specific missing brief or interface contract is retained.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained task state in one process and used local helper scripts for repeated requirement edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material difference is not lost requirement context but the amount of coordination state created by many child executions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a small partial implementation set collected as 28 requirement patch files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented release/changelog/tooling changes and some code fixes, reaching 58 requirement patch files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed roughly twice as many patch artifacts; neither came close to the 773 required changes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ended with workflow_child_logs present but workflow_retrieved_without_stop false, indicating workflow lifecycle did not close cleanly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow calls, child logs, or delegation result lifecycle to join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel attempt had an unfinished workflow result lifecycle; serial closure was a local-agent API error after local work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel introduced shared-workspace child execution guarded by a flock commit helper, but no concrete write collision or overwrite is retained.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made all changes locally and the control records show no workflow child writes or delegation activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried shared-state coordination overhead without a proven collision; serial avoided that surface entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final status reports protocol_ok false and smoke_ok false, and run-tests exited with failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final status reports protocol_ok true and smoke_ok true, but run-tests still exited with failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial met the harness protocol/smoke expectations while parallel failed those checks, though both failed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent millions of workflow-child tokens and hundreds of child tool calls across repeated workflow-heavy rounds, then hit rate-limit/timeout closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent no workflow-child tokens and ended after local continuation hit an API 429 with 58 patches present.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget pressure came from broad fan-out; serial budget pressure came from ordinary single-agent continuation over an oversized backlog.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations have solution_passed false, so this is a both_fail pair rather than a discordant outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is process and coverage: parallel delegated hundreds of one-requirement children and closed with protocol/smoke failure and 28 collected patches, while serial worked without delegation, passed protocol/smoke checks, and reached 58 patches before an API 429. The retained pattern explains a realized adverse parallel coordination consequence but not a pass/fail divergence.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out consumed most of the available budget in child execution and left the workflow lifecycle incomplete.
Only 28 requirement patch files were collected at final parallel harness collection.
Parallel protocol and smoke validation were false.
serial_contributors: Serial had workflows disabled and no delegation, preserving one local execution path.
Serial reached 58 collected requirement patch files and passed protocol/smoke validation before failing official tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions remained far short of the 773 required changes, so many official failures reflect ordinary incomplete implementation coverage.
Serial also ended on an API 429, which limited continuation independent of any parallel coordination pattern.
evaluator_effects: The official result exposes only failed/pass booleans and failed test names in these records; passed and total testcase counts are not resolved by the status parser.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official outcome difference; supported comparative explanation for adverse parallel coverage, protocol, and closure behavior.

candidates.near_match_reason: The unretrieved workflow state is a terminal symptom of the same broad implementation fan-out, not an independent verifier-result handoff failure.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent used a workflow pipeline that created one child per requirement across broad shards, then spent most of the available run in child workflows and ended with unretrieved/stopped workflow state, protocol failure, smoke failure, and only partial patch coverage. The serial control did not delegate and produced more patch files locally, so this is a realized adverse parallel orchestration pattern but not an official outcome differential because both failed.
